description: Part B lifecycle scenarios (SPEC-v2 §6.9, §7). Replay each scenario against a fresh in-memory reference store whose authoritative clock starts at start_time, whose evaluator lease is lease_seconds, and whose receipt log log_id is signed by verifier_key. Requests use the verifier-ordering input schema; the request's now is always the store clock at the step.

semantics.abandon: the receipt-abandonment procedure: freeze the receipt log and mark every claim whose outbox entry was not appended receipt_abandoned; expect abandoned (request names in log order)
semantics.acknowledge: submit the request's last published receipt to the reference checkpoint directly as Acknowledge(log_id, sequence, previous_receipt_hash, entry_hash). mode exact = the receipt's own entry hash; fork = the same tuple with the first entry-hash byte flipped. Expect ack_timestamp, or failed=true when the checkpoint refuses. A different entry hash at an acknowledged sequence is a fork: the checkpoint freezes the log and acknowledges nothing further for it, including the publisher's own submissions (SPEC-v2 §7.8)
semantics.claim_only: preflight and claim without evaluating (an evaluator that crashed after claiming); expect disposition or error_class. The harness keeps the evaluator owner token the claim store returned for a later finalize step
semantics.corrupt_state: alter one byte of the request's sealed terminal result in the primary store
semantics.device_power_loss: arm a power loss for the next submission only: before_commit records nothing; after_commit records the acknowledgement durably but loses the response
semantics.device_resubmit: retry the exact tuple for sequence; expect ack_time (the original acknowledgement time on an identical retry) or device_error
semantics.device_startup: before serving, check in order: a frozen component (checkpoint_frozen); fewer appended receipt-log entries than the component acknowledged (primary_behind: rollback or lost state); a recomputed complete-state digest that differs from the anchored one (state_digest_mismatch, including a rollback that kept the receipt-log prefix); otherwise ready
semantics.device_submit: submit, in log order, every appended entry of the primary that the component has not acknowledged with the same entry hash; expect acknowledged (the sequences acknowledged by this call) and device_error for the failure that stopped it: power_loss, storage_full, state_mismatch (the submission does not extend the head or its state is not the anchored state), frozen (a different entry at an acknowledged sequence; the component freezes), or clock_regressed
semantics.finalize: call the claim store's finalize operation directly for the request's claim with the owner token from its claim_only step, terminal_b64 as the terminal result, body_b64 as the receipt outbox body and allow_valid_until (0 unless an allow); expect finalize_result committed (true) or identical (false, the same result already committed), or error_class. The store binds the body to the sealed claim (SPEC-v2 §7.5): a refused finalize commits nothing
semantics.ledger_execute: atomically mark set (default: the last set opened) executed at the store clock; expect ledger_error incomplete, expired (an approval is no longer Allowed), already_executed, or none
semantics.ledger_execute_concurrent: count concurrent executions of the set; expect executed, the number that succeeded
semantics.ledger_open: open approval_set: agent_key and root_keys name keys.json fixture keys whose complete public keys the set pins (roots in slot order); request_hash_b64 is the action's operation-context hash. The ledger derives the expected session context from verifier_id, workspace_id, the agent key ID, session_id, invocation_id = id, and request_hash (§2.4); session_context_b64 is that derivation as a known answer and is never a ledger input. Expect ledger_error approval_set_invalid when the set is malformed or names one root key twice
semantics.ledger_record: record the request's released decision (from its last release step; none if that release was not released) and its exact bundle in slot of set (default: the last set opened). Checks in order: not_released (not a released allow); action_mismatch (receipt bundle_hash differs from the bundle); approval_reused (the claim is already recorded in another approval set); action_mismatch (receipt or bundle verifier, receipt or bundle agent ID, bundle agent key, receipt required scope, or bundle session_context differs from the set and its derived context); root_mismatch (the chain's terminal issuer key is not the slot's pinned root key, or the receipt's issuer_ids omit it); slot_filled. Expect ledger_complete or that ledger_error
semantics.ledger_record_concurrent: record requests[i] in slot i concurrently; expect ledger_complete for the final state
semantics.plant_release: write a release record for the request's claim directly into primary storage, bypassing release and anchoring: it names the claim's appended receipt entry hash and the acknowledgement timestamp time (a primary-storage compromise)
semantics.profile dual_root: one verifier and receipt log; each request pins exactly one trusted root. An application approval ledger records released decisions per approval set
semantics.profile single_device_offline: the primary is the reference store plus an anchored SecurityJournalV2 store, a challenge issuance store, and device.replay_epoch; its complete-state digest is SHA-384 over the versioned canonical projection of SPEC-v2 §7.13. The store never acknowledges its own entries; the checkpoint is an independent monotonic authenticated component on the same device (seed and capacity from device) that is provisioned with the primary's initial digest, anchors the primary's new complete-state digest before every durable security-state change takes effect (a change whose previous digest differs from the anchored one is refused and undone, so a verify fails before claim with claim_store_unavailable), records per receipt-log entry the entry hash and the anchored digest, signs every acknowledgement with its own key, and reads the same security clock as the store. rate_at_finalization makes the store admit max_rate inside finalization, as in scenarios
semantics.profile_scenarios: SPEC-v2 §7.13 and §7.14 profile scripts. Each starts from a fresh reference store (as for scenarios) and adds the test-only component its profile names. Steps use the lifecycle ops (set_time, set_ack_withheld, verify, publish, release) plus the profile ops below; release checkpoint device = the device component, reference = the store checkpoint
semantics.publish: drain the outbox for the request's committed outcome; the reference store assigns each receipt-log position at terminal commit, in commit order. mode ok = reference publisher; signer_failure = the signer fails for this call and appends nothing; corrupt_signature = the published receipt with one Ed25519 signature byte flipped. Expect receipt_sequence, or failed=true with publish_error head_of_line_blocked (an earlier entry is unpublished), signer_unavailable, or log_frozen
semantics.rate_at_finalization: scenario flag: the reference store admits the sealed max_rate batch inside the finalization compare-and-set and is used as both claim store and rate store. This is the single-store max_rate implementation of SPEC-v2 §7.6: an allow is counted at T_final in the same transaction that commits it, all counters of the sealed batch or none, and every other terminal result, including recovery's evaluation_interrupted, counts nothing
semantics.recover: RecoverInterruptedClaim for the request's claim ID (ProtocolClaimID of the request's verifier namespace, replay epoch and challenge, whether or not it was ever claimed): the store returns the sealed claim, T_claim and the last recorded evaluation progress (refusing while the lease is live), and the evaluation_interrupted receipt reports that progress per dimension; expect stage committed (idempotent for the same body) with its assessments, or error_class
semantics.recover_direct: call the claim store's recovery operation directly for the request's claim (from its claim_only step) with terminal_b64 as the terminal result and body_b64 as the receipt outbox body, after the evaluator lease expired; expect finalize_result committed (true) or identical (false, the same result already committed), or error_class. The store validates the result and body exactly as finalize does (SPEC-v2 §7.5: malformed for a body that is not a canonical receipt body, configuration_invalid for a body that does not bind the sealed claim or a result that differs from it) and accepts only indeterminate/evaluation_interrupted (configuration_invalid otherwise): a refused recovery commits nothing
semantics.release: ReleaseV2Decision with the request's committed outcome and its last published receipt (none when not published or when mode is no_receipt, or receipt_of another request). checkpoint reference = the store checkpoint; wrong_entry = acknowledgements report a different entry hash. Expect release_status, release_reason, decision, release_time. A withheld result at release steps 7 or 8 is recorded in the claim store when no release is recorded yet, and every later release of that claim returns the recorded withheld result right after step 1; rejected describes only that call (SPEC-v2 §6.9)
semantics.release_forged: ReleaseV2Decision with a committed outcome that was never produced by the verifier (zero value); always rejected
semantics.restore: mode snapshot = replace the primary with the named copy (a rollback) and bind it to the same component without provisioning; the component and the clock are unchanged
semantics.resume: ResumeCommittedClaim for the request's claim ID (computed as for recover): the store returns the claim's persisted terminal record and the implementation returns its committed handoff, which replaces any handoff the harness holds for the request, so later publish and release steps use it (SPEC-v2 §7.11). Expect stage committed with decision, decision_reason and allow_horizon (0 when absent), or error_class: claim_not_found for a claim the store does not hold, claim_lease_live for a claim still evaluating under a live lease, claim_lease_lost for one still evaluating after its lease expired
semantics.set_ack_withheld: withheld=true stops the reference outbox from submitting appended entries to the checkpoint; withheld=false submits every pending entry in log order at the current clock
semantics.set_time: set the authoritative clock (it may move backward to exercise clock regression). The store keeps a high-water mark of every authoritative reading, including the checkpoint's acknowledgement timestamps, and a reading below it is a reported clock regression
semantics.snapshot: copy the complete primary state (store, journal, issuance records) under snapshot
semantics.stage_status: stage the request's status keys (configured in ascending issuer order) and journal preload into the primary's anchored SecurityJournalV2 store, as before disconnection; each journal transition is anchored
semantics.upload: outbox upload after reconnection: send each signed receipt of the component-acknowledged prefix once, in log order; expect uploaded. Upload never releases or changes a release
semantics.verifier_configuration: status keys, status policy, trust, journal setup and evidence come from each request exactly as in verifier-ordering.json
semantics.verify: VerifyProofBundleV2 against the store; expect stage, error_class, disposition; for committed, decision/decision_reason are read from the committed receipt body for the test only, and allow_horizon is the handoff value
semantics.verify modes: verify with mode expire_lease_during_status sets the store clock to time when the status provider is first called (the evaluator lease expires mid-lookup); recover_during_status additionally runs recover for the same claim there and checks expect.recovered (the late evaluator is then fenced); regress_clock_during_status sets the clock to time (below T_claim) there; cancel_before_claim calls verify with the caller's cancellation already signalled, so the verifier stops before the claim and nothing is consumed; cancel_during_status signals the caller's cancellation when the status provider is first called and the provider then reports that cancellation as its result (SPEC-v2 §6.11)
semantics.verify_concurrent: run verify for every request in requests concurrently against the store at the current clock, each with its own callbacks; expect.outcomes is the sorted multiset of results, each the stage alone for committed and replay, or stage/error_class for preflight and evaluating

scenarios.name: allow_published_acknowledged_released
scenarios.description: verify commits a non-actionable allow; publication and acknowledgement release it; a second release is idempotent and appends nothing

scenarios.name: release_without_receipt_is_pending
scenarios.description: a committed allow without a published receipt is pending, never released (Part A to Part B downgrade attempt)

scenarios.name: release_without_acknowledgement_is_pending_then_late_ack_releases
scenarios.description: an appended but unacknowledged receipt is pending; a late acknowledgement before every deadline releases it at the acknowledgement time

scenarios.name: late_ack_at_challenge_expiry_is_withheld
scenarios.description: an acknowledgement timestamped at the challenge expiry can never release (exclusive deadline)

scenarios.name: release_one_second_before_challenge_expiry
scenarios.description: release at expires_at - 1 succeeds

scenarios.name: release_at_challenge_expiry_is_withheld
scenarios.description: release at exactly expires_at is withheld even with an earlier acknowledgement

scenarios.name: release_at_allow_horizon_is_withheld
scenarios.description: an allow whose status horizon is Now+1 is withheld when released at exactly Now+1

scenarios.name: release_before_allow_horizon
scenarios.description: the same allow released at Now, before its Now+1 horizon, is released

scenarios.name: signer_failure_then_retry
scenarios.description: a publisher (signer) failure appends nothing and release stays pending; a retry publishes and releases

scenarios.name: corrupt_receipt_signature_is_rejected
scenarios.description: a published receipt whose signature does not verify under the configured verifier key is rejected; rejected describes only that call's inputs, so the genuine receipt then releases (SPEC-v2 §6.9)

scenarios.name: receipt_of_another_claim_is_rejected
scenarios.description: a valid receipt for a different committed claim does not bind this claim's body; the rejection is per call, so this claim's own receipt then releases

scenarios.name: acknowledgement_for_another_entry_is_rejected
scenarios.description: an acknowledgement whose entry hash differs from the verified receipt is a fork signal and is rejected; the rejection records nothing for the claim, so a call through the genuine checkpoint releases

scenarios.name: planted_release_record_does_not_replace_acknowledgement
scenarios.description: a release record written into the claim store with the appended receipt's entry hash and a plausible acknowledgement time is not evidence of acknowledgement: release stays pending while the entry is unacknowledged, and once acknowledged at a different time the planted record is a release_state_mismatch

scenarios.name: repeated_release_reverifies_acknowledgement
scenarios.description: a repeated release of an already released claim obtains the acknowledgement again: an acknowledgement for a different entry is rejected rather than answered from the release record

scenarios.name: forged_committed_outcome_is_rejected
scenarios.description: an application cannot release a committed outcome the verifier did not produce

scenarios.name: clock_regression_at_release_is_withheld
scenarios.description: a release reading earlier than the acknowledgement time is a clock regression; the withheld result is recorded and is permanent, so a later release after the clock passes the acknowledgement time is still withheld (SPEC-v2 §6.9)

scenarios.name: recorded_withheld_answers_before_receipt_checks
scenarios.description: once a withheld result is recorded, every later release of the claim returns it right after the committed-state step: without a receipt it is withheld rather than pending, and with a mismatched acknowledgement it is withheld rather than rejected

scenarios.name: withheld_after_recorded_release_records_nothing
scenarios.description: a release record already present is the first record and wins: a later call whose clock reading regressed is withheld for that call only, and a call with a current clock returns the recorded release again

scenarios.name: crash_after_claim_lease_recovery
scenarios.description: an evaluator that crashes after claiming leaves the claim in progress; recovery is refused while the lease is live, then commits evaluation_interrupted, which publishes and releases as a non-actionable indeterminate; recovery is idempotent

scenarios.name: head_of_line_blocking
scenarios.description: receipt-log positions are assigned at terminal commit; a later entry cannot publish while an earlier one is pending, and its release stays pending until it publishes in order

scenarios.name: receipt_abandoned
scenarios.description: abandoning the log marks every committed claim whose receipt was not appended receipt_abandoned: its release is withheld, an exact retry fails before claim with receipt_abandoned, and the frozen log publishes nothing; a receipt appended before abandonment still releases

scenarios.name: lease_expires_during_status_then_recovery
scenarios.description: the evaluator lease expires while the status lookup runs: the next progress write is fenced (claim_lease_lost) and nothing is committed; an exact retry sees the claim in progress; recovery commits evaluation_interrupted with trust trusted and context bound retained and the interrupted status lookup unavailable

scenarios.name: late_worker_fenced_after_recovery
scenarios.description: recovery commits evaluation_interrupted while the original evaluator is still in its status lookup; the late evaluator's next write fails with claim_already_terminal and cannot replace the recovered result

scenarios.name: clock_regression_at_claim
scenarios.description: a store clock below the greatest reading already returned creates no claim and consumes nothing (claim_store_unavailable); once the clock recovers the same request claims and commits

scenarios.name: clock_regression_during_evaluation
scenarios.description: a store clock that moves below T_claim during evaluation fails the next store write with clock_regressed and commits nothing; recovery after the lease commits evaluation_interrupted

scenarios.name: restore_exact_state
scenarios.description: continuing on an exact copy of the complete store state keeps every claim: an exact retry is a terminal replay and the published receipt still releases

scenarios.name: restore_lost_state_with_epoch_bump
scenarios.description: after a restore that lost claim state, the recovery authority advances the replay epoch: a challenge issued in the earlier epoch fails before claim with stale_replay_epoch, and a challenge of the new epoch claims, commits and releases on the new receipt log

scenarios.name: release_of_claim_the_store_does_not_hold
scenarios.description: after a restore that lost claim state, the configured claim store answers that it holds no claim for the earlier handoff (claim_not_found): release rejects it as release_state_mismatch rather than reporting a retryable pending (SPEC-v2 §6.9 step 1)

scenarios.name: rate_admission_at_finalization
scenarios.description: with max_rate admitted inside the finalization compare-and-set, two allows fill a 2-per-60-second counter; the third finalizes once as constraint_denied; a request 60 seconds later is admitted again

scenarios.name: rate_admission_is_all_or_none
scenarios.description: the sealed batch has two counters of one certificate (2 per 120 seconds and 1 per 60 seconds). T2, 30 seconds after T1, is denied by the 60-second counter alone and must not count against the 120-second counter, so T3 at 60 seconds is admitted (with a partial admission it would be denied)

scenarios.name: rate_retry_and_changed_batch_count_once
scenarios.description: an exact retry of an admitted claim is a terminal replay and is not counted again; a different proof whose signed rate batch differs is a replay of the claimed challenge and admits nothing; so one more allow fills the 2-per-60-second counter and the next is denied

scenarios.name: rate_clock_rollback_keeps_admissions_blocking
scenarios.description: two allows admitted at Now+30 fill the counter; with the clock rolled back to Now nothing is claimed or admitted (claim_store_unavailable); back at Now+30 the admissions still count, and only a reading strictly later than their window (Now+90) admits again

scenarios.name: rate_counts_only_allow
scenarios.description: terminal results other than allow count nothing: an indeterminate (trust_unavailable) and a claim recovered as evaluation_interrupted after its evaluator crashed leave the 2-per-60-second counter empty, so two allows are admitted and only the third is denied

scenarios.name: different_proof_for_claimed_challenge_is_replay
scenarios.description: a second, different proof for an already claimed challenge is rejected before claim without disclosure and does not advance the stream

scenarios.name: stream_sequence_rules
scenarios.description: first sequence must be 1; exact retries replay without advancing; duplicates, gaps and reorders fail before claim with stream_sequence_mismatch; of two claims with the same sequence exactly one commits

scenarios.name: cancel_before_claim_consumes_nothing
scenarios.description: a caller that cancels before the claim consumes nothing: verify fails before claim with evaluation_cancelled, no claim exists to recover (claim_not_found), and the same proof then claims, commits and releases

scenarios.name: cancel_after_claim_keeps_claim_recoverable
scenarios.description: a caller that cancels during the status lookup stops evaluation with nothing committed (evaluation_cancelled); the claim stays in progress for exact retries, recovery is refused while the lease is live, and lease-expiry recovery commits evaluation_interrupted with the cancelled lookup unavailable, which publishes and releases as a non-actionable indeterminate

scenarios.name: concurrent_stream_advances
scenarios.description: two different proofs carrying stream_seq 2 for one stream key are verified concurrently after sequence 1: claims are serialized per stream key, so exactly one commits and the other fails before claim with stream_sequence_mismatch; the stream then accepts only sequence 3

scenarios.name: outbox_retained_past_challenge_expiry
scenarios.description: a committed allow whose signer fails stays in the receipt outbox past challenge expiry: publication at the expiry still appends the identical sealed body at sequence 1, release is withheld as challenge_expired, and an exact retry after expiry fails before claim

scenarios.name: checkpoint_fork_freezes_log
scenarios.description: an identical acknowledgement retry returns the original timestamp; a different entry hash at an acknowledged sequence is refused as a fork and freezes the log, so the next correctly linked entry is never acknowledged (neither by the publisher's submission nor directly) and its release stays pending

scenarios.name: checkpoint_refusal_without_fork_does_not_freeze
scenarios.description: an out-of-order acknowledgement is refused without freezing the log: the entries are then acknowledged in order and release

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_verifier_id
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose verifier_id names another verifier key (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_agent_id
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose agent_id names another agent (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_bundle_hash
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose bundle_hash names request B's proof bundle (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_issuer_ids
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose issuer_ids omits one sealed issuer (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_required_scope
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose required_scope is data:write while the claim sealed data:read (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_context_policy_digest
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose context_policy_digest is another policy's digest (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_constraint_evaluators
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose constraint_evaluators lists an evaluator the sealed snapshot does not contain (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_other_terminal_decision
scenarios.description: the claim store refuses to finalize a canonical receipt body whose the terminal result is deny/delegation_revoked while the body is indeterminate/status_unavailable (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once, an identical retry is a no-op, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_null_context_policy_digest_unverified
scenarios.description: the claim sealed a context policy, and the canonical receipt body records context_assessment unverified with a null context_policy_digest: the claim store refuses it (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_null_context_policy_digest_unbound
scenarios.description: the claim sealed a context policy, and the canonical receipt body records context_assessment unbound with a null context_policy_digest: the claim store refuses it (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_allow_without_allow_horizon
scenarios.description: a canonical allow receipt body finalized with allow_valid_until 0 is refused (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §6.8, §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_negative_allow_horizon_on_non_allow
scenarios.description: an indeterminate receipt body finalized with allow_valid_until -1 is refused (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §6.8): a non-allow carries exactly 0; the same body with 0 then finalizes once

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_allow_horizon_beyond_timestamp_domain
scenarios.description: an allow receipt body finalized with allow_valid_until 253402300800 is refused (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §2.5, §6.8): every horizon is clamped to 253402300799; the genuine indeterminate body then finalizes once

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_allow_horizon_on_non_allow
scenarios.description: an indeterminate receipt body finalized with a positive allow_valid_until is refused (configuration_invalid, SPEC-v2 §6.8, §7.5) and commits nothing; the same body with no horizon then finalizes once

scenarios.name: finalize_rejects_body_with_context_policy_digest_not_evaluated
scenarios.description: the claim sealed a context policy, and the receipt body records context_assessment not_evaluated with the sealed context_policy_digest: that body is not a receipt body (SPEC-v2 §5.8), so the claim store refuses it as malformed (SPEC-v2 §7.5) and commits nothing; the genuine body then finalizes once

scenarios.name: resume_finalized_claim_without_handoff
scenarios.description: a result committed by a direct finalize has no handoff; resumption returns it from the store, and it is published and released like a returned handoff (SPEC-v2 §7.11)

scenarios.name: resume_replaces_lost_allow_handoff
scenarios.description: resuming a committed allow returns the same handoff: the same allow horizon, published at the same position and released once

scenarios.name: resume_refuses_claims_without_a_committed_record
scenarios.description: resumption never commits: an unknown claim is claim_not_found, a claim evaluating under a live lease is claim_lease_live and after it claim_lease_lost; after lease-expiry recovery it resumes the interrupted result

scenarios.name: recover_rejects_malformed_body
scenarios.description: after the evaluator lease expired, the claim store's recovery operation receives the canonical interrupted result with a receipt body that is not a canonical receipt body ({"decision":"allow","verifier_id":"forged"}): it is malformed (SPEC-v2 §7.5, §7.7); the refused recovery commits nothing, so the canonical interrupted recovery then commits, publishes at sequence 1, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: recover_rejects_body_for_another_claim
scenarios.description: after the evaluator lease expired, the claim store's recovery operation receives a canonical interrupted receipt body whose bundle_hash names request B's proof bundle: it does not bind the sealed claim and is configuration_invalid (SPEC-v2 §7.5); the refused recovery commits nothing, so the canonical interrupted recovery then commits, publishes at sequence 1, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: recover_rejects_context_policy_digest_not_evaluated
scenarios.description: after the evaluator lease expired, the claim store's recovery operation receives an interrupted receipt body with context_assessment not_evaluated and the sealed context_policy_digest: that body is not a receipt body (SPEC-v2 §5.8), so recovery refuses it as malformed (SPEC-v2 §7.5); the refused recovery commits nothing, so the canonical interrupted recovery then commits, publishes at sequence 1, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: recover_rejects_other_decision
scenarios.description: after the evaluator lease expired, the claim store's recovery operation receives a canonical receipt body bound to the sealed claim and a matching terminal result, both indeterminate/status_unavailable: recovery commits only indeterminate/evaluation_interrupted, so it is configuration_invalid (SPEC-v2 §7.5); the refused recovery commits nothing, so the canonical interrupted recovery then commits, publishes at sequence 1, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: recover_rejects_terminal_result_other_than_body
scenarios.description: after the evaluator lease expired, the claim store's recovery operation receives the canonical interrupted receipt body with a terminal result naming deny/delegation_revoked: the result differs from the body and is configuration_invalid (SPEC-v2 §7.5); the refused recovery commits nothing, so the canonical interrupted recovery then commits, publishes at sequence 1, and an exact retry of the proof is a terminal replay

scenarios.name: recover_direct_accepts_canonical_interrupted_body
scenarios.description: after the evaluator lease expired, the claim store's recovery operation commits the canonical interrupted result and receipt body for the sealed claim; an identical repeat is a no-op, the recovery helper builds the same bytes and returns the committed result, and the receipt publishes at sequence 1

scenarios.name: recover_direct_accepts_terminal_result_with_other_members
scenarios.description: a terminal result whose decision and decision_reason match the canonical interrupted body, with further members of any JSON type, is committed by the claim store's recovery operation exactly as finalization would commit it; an identical repeat is a no-op

profile_scenarios.name: device_release_requires_component_ack
profile_scenarios.description: a committed and appended allow stays pending until the on-device component acknowledges it; the acknowledgement releases it and the uplink sends the receipt

profile_scenarios.name: device_power_loss_before_ack
profile_scenarios.description: power fails before the component commits: nothing is recorded and release stays pending; after restart the primary matches the component head and the retried submission releases at its own acknowledgement time

profile_scenarios.name: device_power_loss_after_ack
profile_scenarios.description: power fails after the component commits: the acknowledgement is durable though its response was lost, so release uses the original acknowledgement time and an identical resubmission returns the same acknowledgement

profile_scenarios.name: device_primary_rollback
profile_scenarios.description: the primary is restored to a state before an acknowledged entry: startup reports primary_behind, and the rolled-back primary cannot claim a challenge because its state does not extend the anchored state

profile_scenarios.name: device_state_digest_mismatch
profile_scenarios.description: the primary's sealed state changes outside an anchored change after acknowledgement: startup reports state_digest_mismatch and the primary cannot claim another challenge

profile_scenarios.name: device_rollback_loses_consumed_challenge
profile_scenarios.description: with the receipt log unchanged, a restore loses a later consumed challenge: the claim was anchored when it was made, so startup reports state_digest_mismatch and the challenge cannot be claimed again

profile_scenarios.name: device_rollback_loses_stream_advance
profile_scenarios.description: with the receipt log unchanged, a restore loses a stream advance from sequence 1 to 2: startup reports state_digest_mismatch and the lost sequence cannot be claimed again

profile_scenarios.name: device_rollback_loses_journal_state
profile_scenarios.description: with the receipt log and claims unchanged, a restore rolls back status evidence staged into the anchored journal: startup reports state_digest_mismatch

profile_scenarios.name: device_planted_release_record
profile_scenarios.description: primary storage gains a release record naming the appended but unacknowledged receipt entry with a plausible acknowledgement time: release still obtains the component acknowledgement and stays pending, and the record is outside the anchored state, so startup reports state_digest_mismatch and no further claim is made

profile_scenarios.name: device_altered_release_record
profile_scenarios.description: after an anchored release, primary storage rewrites the release record with a different plausible acknowledgement time: a repeated release compares it with the component acknowledgement and is rejected, and startup reports state_digest_mismatch

profile_scenarios.name: device_rollback_loses_release_record
profile_scenarios.description: with the receipt log unchanged, a restore loses an anchored release record: startup reports state_digest_mismatch, and recording the release again does not extend the anchored state, so release stays pending

profile_scenarios.name: device_checkpoint_storage_full
profile_scenarios.description: a component with room for one acknowledgement refuses the second entry without overwriting the first: the second release stays pending and the first still releases

profile_scenarios.name: device_staged_status_goes_stale
profile_scenarios.description: status staged before disconnection supports an allow until its next_update; offline at that deadline the same staged evidence is stale, so the next decision is a non-actionable indeterminate

profile_scenarios.name: device_rtc_regression
profile_scenarios.description: the device clock moves backward: the component cannot acknowledge, a new claim is refused, and a release reading below the acknowledgement time is withheld; the withheld result is recorded, so once the clock recovers the entry stays withheld (SPEC-v2 §6.9) and a later entry acknowledged on the recovered clock releases

profile_scenarios.name: device_rollback_loses_rate_state
profile_scenarios.description: with max_rate admitted at finalization and the receipt log unchanged, a restore loses an admitted rate commit and its claim: startup reports state_digest_mismatch and the lost request cannot be admitted again

profile_scenarios.name: device_offline_recovery_upload
profile_scenarios.description: while the uplink is down the device releases locally; the uplink later sends only the acknowledged prefix, each receipt once; a receipt acknowledged after its challenge expired is uploaded as evidence but stays withheld, because upload is an outbox operation and not a deferred release

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_both_released_executes_once
profile_scenarios.description: root A and root B each release an allow under their own challenge for the same action and approval set; the ledger is incomplete after one, executable after both, and executes once

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_one_root_missing
profile_scenarios.description: only root A has approved: root A's decision cannot fill root B's slot and the action is not executable

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_other_root_missing
profile_scenarios.description: only root B has approved: the action is not executable

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_duplicate_root
profile_scenarios.description: a set naming one root twice is invalid; a second, separately released approval chaining to root A does not count for root B

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_replay
profile_scenarios.description: a root B proof presented on root A's already claimed challenge is a replay before claim; the set stays incomplete

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_mismatched_action
profile_scenarios.description: root B releases an allow for a different action under its own challenge; the ledger refuses it for this set

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_committed_unreleased
profile_scenarios.description: root B's allow is committed and appended but never released (its acknowledgement arrives at challenge expiry); a committed outcome cannot fill a slot

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_concurrent_completion
profile_scenarios.description: both approvals are recorded concurrently and eight concurrent executions race; exactly one executes

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_expired_before_execution
profile_scenarios.description: both approvals are recorded but the action is attempted at the challenge expiry; it is not executable

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_cross_set_reuse
profile_scenarios.description: two approval sets for the same action: the released approvals recorded in the first set cannot be recorded in the second, whose derived context differs and which refuses any claim already counted elsewhere; only the first set executes

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_same_set_different_action
profile_scenarios.description: a set with the same approval_set_id, verifier, session and agent but a different action request hash derives a different context: approvals released for the first action do not fill it

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_swapped_verifier
profile_scenarios.description: a root A approval whose session context was derived for a different verifier ID is refused although the receipt's verifier is correct; the approval for the derived context fills the slot

profile_scenarios.name: dual_root_set_names_other_verifier
profile_scenarios.description: a set naming a different verifier derives a different context and does not match the receipts' verifier: released approvals for this verifier do not fill it
